subject: NAMO_TURN_DETECTOR_V1_MULTILINGUAL
hypothesis: On real German human-to-agent pauses, NAMO semantic EOU can move the endpointing Pareto frontier below the identical silence/VAD-only baseline, reducing dead air at a fixed false-cutoff budget.
counterhypothesis: NAMO's reported German classification metrics do not transfer to causal real-conversation endpointing because ASR-prefix lag/instability and mid-turn hesitation patterns erase the semantic advantage; the VAD-only policy remains equal or better after latency is accounted for.
discriminator: Run the same pinned German eot-bench silence spans through the VAD-only policy and NAMO semantic EOU, sweep policy thresholds/action-delay/timeout, and compare false-cutoff versus endpoint-latency Pareto frontiers.
required_evidence: exact dataset revision and consumed-data manifest/hash
per-span predictions bound to dataset IDs and timestamps
false-cutoff/latency operating points and Pareto frontier
routing: Trigger4 owns target execution/integration/acceptance. Trigger7 owns source pin, falsifiable benchmark contract and post-result research interpretation.
